name: The Tides Inn
positioning: Waterfront resort on a tributary of the Chesapeake Bay in coastal Virginia, open since 1947, with a marina, a beach and hands-on ecology experiences on Carter's Creek
best_for: Families and multi-generational groups wanting connected rooms by the water
Travelers who want hands-on Chesapeake experiences such as oystering, crabbing and river cruises
Boaters arriving by water, with an overnight marina for sail-in guests

facts.text: The Tides Inn is a waterfront resort on a tributary of the Chesapeake Bay.
The resort is just under three hours from Washington, DC and one hour from Richmond.
The Tides Inn opened to the public on July 15, 1947.
In the early 1940s, the land the Tides Inn sits on was known as the Ashburn Farm.
A twenty-seven-slip overnight marina welcomes sail-in guests.
All Water View rooms have views of the shoreline, beach or marina.
Connected two- and three-bedroom rooms and suites come in a variety of bed and balcony configurations.
On the Mighty Rappahannock cruise, Captain Bull shares the history of the Rappahannock River aboard the Lil' Tip-Sea.
In the Beautiful Swimmers blue crab experience, guests learn how to set and pull crab pots.
Salt & Meadow draws heirloom vegetables, herbs and honey daily from the five-acre Tides Inn Farm.
Handcrafted wooden liquor lockers from the hotel's early days still line the walls of Salt & Meadow Restaurant.

highlights.text: A $3.6 million shoreline restoration project added a Shoreline Trail along Carter's Creek, surrounded by an oyster reef and wetland grasses.
In the Watermen's Experience, guests haul oyster cages with the resort's resident ecologist.
Coastal Seaplane Experiences offers seaplane tours boarding at the Tides Inn Beach, taking off and landing on Carter's Creek.
The resort has signature lime-green cruise bikes for exploring the town.

considerations.text: A daily resort fee applies; it includes the fitness center, beach and pool access, tennis and pickleball.
The Historical Garden Tour is seasonal, offered from June 10 through October 15.
WhataHotel notes a remote location in the Northern Neck region.
